item.content:encoded:
Trump approved Flávio Bolsonaro's US entry after Brazil election loss: Reports US President Donald Trump approved allowing Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to enter the United States following his defeat in Brazil's presidential election, a Trump adviser told CNN, while Brazilian news site, Bahia Notícias reported that Washington would grant visas to the senator and his family. ANI | Updated: 28-10-2026 09:43 IST | Created: 28-10-2026 09:43 IST

Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

US President Donald Trump approved allowing Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to enter the United States following his defeat in Brazil's presidential election, a Trump adviser told CNN, while Brazilian news site, Bahia Notícias reported that Washington would grant visas to the senator and his family. According to CNN, Trump administration officials were aware on Monday (local time) that Bolsonaro had approximately 24 hours to surrender his passport under a Brazilian Supreme Court order and made clear that he would be allowed to enter the United States. Two US officials told CNN that visas were being issued to Bolsonaro and his family. Brazilian news outlet Bahia Notícias, citing information confirmed by a White House official to Folha de S Paulo on Tuesday, also reported that the US government was aware of the senator's trip and would grant visas to the family. According to people close to the Bolsonaro family, the senator arrived in the United States at around 4:20 pm, accompanied by his wife, Fernanda, and their two daughters. His departure came two days after he lost the presidential election to Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Brazilian news outlet Bahia Notícias, citing sources familiar with the operation, reported that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio was involved in facilitating Bolsonaro's departure. CNN reported that it remained unclear whether Trump and Bolsonaro had spoken directly by phone before the senator left Brazil. The departure followed an order by Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes directing Bolsonaro to surrender his passports within 24 hours. According to CNN, Bolsonaro had denied intending to flee the country in a video posted on Instagram on Monday (local time). CNN reported that the senator is under investigation by Brazil's highest court over alleged corruption, money laundering and currency evasion. The investigations include allegations linked to online betting platforms and the financing of a biopic about his father, former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro. Flávio Bolsonaro denies wrongdoing. CNN reported that no arrest warrant had been issued against him at the time of his departure. Meanwhile, Brazilian President Lula criticised Bolsonaro's reported departure while addressing supporters outside the Palácio da Alvorada on Tuesday (local time), during celebrations marking his 81st birthday. According to Brazilian news outlet Bahia Notícias, Lula called the senator's departure a "shameful act" and said he should have surrendered his passport in compliance with the court's order. "The citizen who leaves their country in secret does so because they owe something," Lula said, according to Brazilian media. Drawing a comparison with his own legal proceedings during Operation Lava Jato, Lula said he had chosen to remain in Brazil and surrender to the Federal Police when he faced accusations. "I decided to turn myself in to the Federal Police because I wanted to unmask my accusers and prove my innocence," Lula said, according to Bahia Notícias. Brazilian news outlet CNN Brasil also reported that Lula criticised Bolsonaro's departure, saying the senator could have remained in the country to address the allegations against him. The reported departure appeared to have surprised members of Bolsonaro's political camp. His campaign manager, Rogerio Marinho, told reporters that the opposition had expected the senator to assume a leadership role after the election. "We're surprised because yesterday we talked about the need for Flávio -- given the roughly 60 million votes he received -- to take on this leadership role for the opposition," Marinho said, according to CNN. The episode follows the departure of Bolsonaro's father, Jair Bolsonaro, for Orlando, Florida, after losing Brazil's 2022 presidential election. Jair Bolsonaro was subsequently sentenced to 27 years in prison over efforts to overturn the election results. Brazilian media reported that Flávio Bolsonaro was expected to address the press on Wednesday (local time), although the location had not been disclosed. (ANI)

item.title: Robert Pattinson calls Steven Soderbergh “completely selfless” for helping Matt Reeves finish ‘The Batman Part II’
item.description: Actor Robert Pattinson has praised filmmaker Steven Soderbergh for stepping in to help complete principal photography on ‘The Batman Part II’ while director Matt Reeves takes a temporary break from ...
item.content:encoded:
Robert Pattinson calls Steven Soderbergh “completely selfless” for helping Matt Reeves finish ‘The Batman Part II’ Actor Robert Pattinson has praised filmmaker Steven Soderbergh for stepping in to help complete principal photography on ‘The Batman Part II’ while director Matt Reeves takes a temporary break from filming due to a family matter, Variety reported.  ANI | Updated: 27-10-2026 22:07 IST | Created: 27-10-2026 22:07 IST

Robert Pattinson (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Actor Robert Pattinson has praised filmmaker Steven Soderbergh for stepping in to help complete principal photography on ‘The Batman Part II’ while director Matt Reeves takes a temporary break from filming due to a family matter, Variety reported. In an interview, Pattinson expressed his gratitude to Soderbergh for offering to help Reeves complete the highly anticipated sequel, starring Pattinson as the iconic DC superhero Batman. “I am so happy he’s come on to help Matt," Pattinson said of Soderbergh. “It’s incredibly generous of him, and he’s doing it in the loveliest way. It’s completely selfless,” as per the outlet. The actor added that Reeves had invested considerable effort in the film’s script and that production was nearing completion. “I think Matt had put so much work into the script, and we’re almost done. So for someone to come in and say, ‘I just want to help Matt do it; I want to do it in conjunction with him and just get it to the edit.’ And to have someone who’s as talented as Steven doing it is great,” Pattinson said, according to Variety. When asked about the production schedule, Pattinson indicated that filming had already resumed. “I think they’re in production already. And I’m starting in a couple of days,” he said. Warner Bros. announced on October 5 that production on ‘The Batman Part II’ had been temporarily paused while Reeves focused on a family matter. The studio did not disclose further details about the circumstances. “Production on ‘The Batman Part II’ has been temporarily paused while Matt Reeves focuses on a family matter,” a studio representative said at the time. “Matt has the full support of DC Studios and we look forward to continuing the journey soon.” Reeves subsequently took to his X account to clarify that he remained the director of the film and expressed gratitude to Soderbergh for helping him complete the project. “Just to be clear, I am not leaving ‘The Batman Part II.’ I am profoundly grateful to Steven for coming to my aid during this challenging time to help me finish principal photography. Thank you to all for your concern and well wishes,” Reeves wrote, according to Variety. DC Studios co-chief James Gunn also addressed the change on Threads, reaffirming Reeves' position as director. “Matt is still the director of ‘The Batman 2’ and always will be. I can’t express how profoundly grateful and moved we are by Steven’s offer to help him complete his vision,” Gunn wrote. Soderbergh, meanwhile, said his objective was to ensure that the additional footage blended seamlessly with the material already filmed. “I thought Matt Reeves’ work on ‘The Batman’ was stunning; it was intentional, specific, and rigorously coherent,” Soderbergh said. “The goal here is to work with Matt and his team to generate footage that will integrate seamlessly with what’s already been shot so Matt can properly finish his film.” ‘The Batman Part II’ is scheduled for release on February 18, 2028. No official announcement has been made regarding a change to the release date. Alongside Pattinson, the film features Scarlett Johansson, Sebastian Stan, Charles Dance, Brian Tyree Henry, Colin Farrell as the Penguin, Andy Serkis as Alfred Pennyworth and Jeffrey Wright as Commissioner Gordon, according to Variety. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
China accused of intimidation campaign to isolate Taiwan politician China is facing allegations of attempting to politically isolate Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) legislator and Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen by pressuring celebrities, businesses and professional associates linked to him. ANI | Updated: 27-10-2026 17:49 IST | Created: 27-10-2026 17:49 IST

Representative Image (Photo/Reuters). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

China is facing allegations of attempting to politically isolate Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) legislator and Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen by pressuring celebrities, businesses and professional associates linked to him. The alleged strategy seeks to discourage public figures from supporting Shen amid growing political sensitivities surrounding Taiwan’s relationship with Beijing, as reported by The Taipei Times. According to The Taipei Times, the allegations emerged after Taiwanese television host Kevin Tsai issued a public apology denying support for Taiwanese independence. Tsai had attended the October 4 inauguration of Shen’s campaign headquarters, prompting criticism from Chinese authorities and social media users. In a post published on Chinese social media, Tsai stated that he had never supported Taiwanese independence. A source familiar with national security cases stated that Beijing was targeting entertainers and companies associated with Shen because directly pressuring the candidate through China’s commercial market was difficult. By threatening their business interests, Chinese authorities allegedly hope to discourage others from joining Shen’s campaign and restrict his access to resources and public support. Tsai’s manager said the television host attended Shen’s event to become acquainted with the politician ahead of a possible interview. However, his business partners in China reportedly continued distancing themselves from him. Such pressure could discourage routine professional engagements with political candidates, depriving them of opportunities to communicate their positions and attract supporters. The report also cited China’s 2021 investigation and penalties against Taiwan’s Far Eastern Group. At the time, Beijing’s Taiwan Affairs Office stated that businesses funding individuals it described as advocates of Taiwanese independence could face punishment, including affiliated companies and financial backers, as highlighted by The Taipei Times. Shen questioned the timing of Tsai’s apology, suggesting it might have been influenced by external forces. The statement appeared a day before Shen’s electoral rival, Taipei Mayor Chiang Wan-an of the Kuomintang (KMT), was scheduled to inaugurate his campaign headquarters, as reported by The Taipei Times. (ANI)
